text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — during the canary I noticed requests routed through sa-proxy are losing project attribution. Quota shows as 'unknown-project' in the dashboard. Anyone else seeing this?
Samir Patel: That's the origin header mapping? which header are you forwarding? @Maria
Maria Chen: We forward `X-RW-Origin: project:proj-123` or `X-RW-Origin: sa:service-abc` (we added this for proxying). The gateway is supposed to canonicalize to origin_claim but appears to be dropped before the quota aggregator.
Lee Wong: Hmm, we changed routing earlier to prefer origin header over token claims for faster lookups. Maybe aggregator reads token claim only.
Ankur Malhotra: Are these requests hitting edge router A or B? we had a sticky change last week.
Maria Chen: Mostly A. I pulled a trace:
```
edge -> auth-proxy (X-RW-Origin set)
auth-proxy -> router A (header present)
router A -> quota-agg (header missing)
```
Samir Patel: rachel-bot said deploy happened to router A at 12:03 — sticky header-policy v2. Could be related.
Rachel-bot: deploy-bot: updated router A config `header-policy=v2` at 2024-11-12T12:03:12Z
Samir Patel: Ok likely regression in auth-proxy -> aggregator relay. Two quick mitigation options: 1) ensure auth-proxy sets internal header `X-RW-Origin-Canonical` before forwarding 2) make aggregator fallback to `X-RW-Origin` if token claim absent.
Lee Wong: Telemetry note: current dashboard counts by claim principal only. If we start reading header we must add a sanitization/validation step to avoid forged headers. Need signed header or exchange.
Maria Chen: We do use a signed header with HMAC in `X-RW-Origin-Sig` when proxy forwards. Did we forget to validate?
Ankur Malhotra: I think proxy sends sig but auth-proxy didn't validate sig after the sticky routing change. Quick grep of logs shows `signature-check: disabled` on auth-proxy for router A.
Samir Patel: Disabling sig check is risky. Why was it disabled? we toggled it in canary to test latency impact.
Maria Chen: Proposal: re-enable sig check in auth-proxy but accept both token claims and header (use header only if sig is valid). That should be safe and restore attribution.
Lee Wong: Also need dashboard tweak: show `attribution_source` (token vs header) and add telemetry tag `origin_source=header|token`. Otherwise it's opaque to support.
Ankur Malhotra: For quota enforcement: prefer project from token when available; use header only if token absent and sig ok. Avoid double counting by normalizing to a single `resolved_project` field. We'll need to update aggregator to dedupe.
Samir Patel: I'll open a small PR to re-enable sig checks and add header pass-through in aggregator. Can we canary at 3% traffic on router A?
Maria Chen: Yes. Also we should emit an event `auth.origin_resolution` with fields `resolved_project`, `source`, `validated_sig` so SRE can track any weirdness.
Lee Wong: Prefer not to ship schema change without updating the schema registry. I'll add the event schema and docs.
Samir Patel: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/452 — includes unit + e2e tests and a small aggregator fallback. Tests include synthetic where header present but sig invalid.
Ankur Malhotra: After canary, run a synthetic suite that sends forged `X-RW-Origin` and invalid `X-RW-Origin-Sig` to confirm aggregator rejects header-based attribution when sig invalid.
Maria Chen: Agreed. Also console UX ask: expose a "preview attribution" when you click a request trace to show which identity (token vs header) would be used for quota. That will save support time.
Lee Wong: I'll add a frontend flag `showAttributionPreview` and a tiny tooltip: `Attribution: token (preferred) | header (sig validated)`
Samir Patel: Rolling tonight. I'll start the canary at 03:00 and watch `auth.origin_resolution` events. Ping me if you want to join the watch.
Maria Chen: thanks :thumbsup:
Deploy-bot: canary started on router A — 3% traffic — job 1765440000
Samir Patel: Canary looks ok so far, no increase in 4xx and `resolved_project` is populated for synthetic requests.
Rachel-bot: deploy-bot: canary success — metrics show auth failures stable; promoted to 20% at 1765441800
Ankur Malhotra: Post-canary checklist: run forged header test, update schema registry, add dashboard column `Origin Source`, and ship console preview.
Maria Chen: I'll create follow-up tickets and assign. Thanks all.
Samir Patel: Nice teamwork.
Maria Chen: closing the thread — will post final rollout note in release channel.
